{{Current events header|2016|06|13}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2016 Orlando nightclub shooting]]
**City officials in [[Orlando, Florida]], continue to identify the bodies of the victims in yesterday's attack. So far, 33 of the reported 49 victims have been identified and their families notified. [http://www.cityoforlando.net/blog/victims/ (City of Orlando)]
**[[Pope Francis]] condemns 'senseless hatred' over a massacre in Orlando, and Archbishop [[Joseph Edward Kurtz|Joseph Kurtz]] of [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Louisville|Louisville, Kentucky]], says "Our prayers are with the victims, their families and all those affected by this terrible act." [http://www.catholicherald.co.uk/news/2016/06/13/pope-francis-condemns-senseless-hatred-of-orlando-massacre/ (Catholic Herald)]
*[[Moro Conflict]]
**[[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] says his government has "compelling reason to believe" that Robert Hall, who was held hostage in the Philippines, has been killed by his captors, presumably the same [[Abu Sayyaf]] militants who beheaded another [[Canada|Canadian]], [[John Ridsdel]], on 25 April 2016. [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/68666c34eafa45b1a6529d15ce88e5c5/canada-believes-canadian-hostage-killed-philippines (AP)]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (1978–present)|Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**A car bomb injures at least nine people, three in serious condition,  in the mainly-[[Kurd]]ish southeast region in [[Turkey|Turkey's]] [[Tunceli Province]]. The explosion occurred close to housing for courthouse employees in the town of [[Ovacık, Dersim|Ovacik]]. There is  no immediate claim of responsibility  for the attack. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2016/06/car-bomb-rocks-eastern-turkey-160613113123297.html (AL Jazeera)] [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/eb4b085a570044829682fc15ae0b21dc/report-9-injured-car-bomb-explosion-southeast-turkey (AP)]

;Business and economics
*[[Microsoft]] agrees to [[List of mergers and acquisitions by Microsoft|buy]] [[Professional network service|professional networking]] site [[LinkedIn]] for $26.2 billion (£18 billion). [http://www.cnet.com/au/news/microsoft-buys-linkedin-in-26-2bn-deal/ (CNET)]  [http://www.bbc.com/news/business-36519766 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**Police in northern [[Greece]] move  more than 400 [[Syria]]ns and [[Iraq]]is by bus from a makeshift camp near the [[Republic of Macedonia|Macedonian]] border to a shelter near the northern city of [[Thessaloniki]], Greece. More than 50,000 migrants remain stranded in Greece following [[Europe]]an border closures, and the [[European Union|European Union's]] agreement with [[Turkey]]. [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/fd5a0bb87e8d40009883aa00b105d6ce/greece-police-clear-more-migrant-camps-near-border (AP)]
*[[Germany–Turkey relations]]
**Eleven [[Turks in Germany|Turkish]]-[[Germans|German]] members of Germany's Parliament, the [[Bundestag]], who voted in support of declaring the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman Turks]] slaughter of [[Armenian Genocide|Armenians]] in 1915 a genocide, are under police protection.  The legislators have faced heavy criticism from [[Turkey|Turkish]] officials, as well as from [[Turks in Germany|Turkish Germans]]. [http://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2016/06/12/11-German-MPs-under-police-protection-over-genocide-squabble-with-Turkey/5841465775367/?spt=hs&or=tn_int (UPI)] [http://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2016/06/09/Turkey-plans-retaliatory-measures-for-German-genocide-resolution-Erdogan-says/8101465480660/?st_rec=5841465775367 (UPI²)]
*The [[Secretary General of NATO]] [[Jens Stoltenberg]] says that the military alliance plans on sending four multinational battalions to [[Estonia]], [[Latvia]], [[Lithuania]] and [[Poland]] in order to boost their defense. However, Stoltenberg said that the battalions will only be deployed on a rotational basis instead of being based permanently. [http://www.rferl.org/content/nato-baltics-poland-russia-ukraine-battalions/27795258.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)] 

;Law and crime
*A 22-year-old [[Netherlands|Dutch]] woman held in [[Qatar]] for nearly three months after telling police she had been [[rape]]d is released following the court ruling of a one-year suspended prison sentence. The [[Associated Press]] reports it isn't clear, "... what sentence was given to the man she accused of rape."  [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/c9578c3beed745988b95fb277cf2c750/diplomat-qatar-frees-dutch-woman-held-after-rape-report (AP)]
*[[Trial of Oscar Pistorius]]
**[[South Africa]]n [[Paralympic Games|Paralympic]] sprinting medalist [[Oscar Pistorius|Oscar Pistorius's]] sentencing hearing begins. He faces a minimum 15-year jail term since his original manslaughter charge  for the 2013 killing of [[Reeva Steenkamp]] has been upgraded to murder. The hearing is set to last for five days. [http://in.reuters.com/article/safrica-pistorius-sentencing-idINKCN0YZ07O (Reuters)] [http://news.sky.com/story/1669727/oscar-pistorius-faces-sentencing-in-june (Sky News)]
*A hostage-crisis took place in [[Magnanville]] near [[Paris]], [[France]] after the attacker killed a police officer. The attacker held the family of the police officer hostage,ending with the mother dead and the child uninjured. [http://bnonews.com/news/index.php/news/id4573 (BNO news)] [http://www.leparisien.fr/yvelines-78/yvelines-un-policier-poignarde-a-mort-a-magnanville-13-06-2016-5880893.php (Le Parisien)]

;Politics and elections
* The [[United States Supreme Court]] strikes down a [[Puerto Rico]] law that would have allowed it to restructure the debts of its public utilities over the objections of creditors.  Puerto Rico's agencies have a $2 billion debt payment due July 1 and has already defaulted on a $370 million debt payment for its [[Puerto Rico Government Development Bank|Government Development Bank]] back on May 1.  [http://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2016-06-13/puerto-rico-debt-restructuring-law-voided-by-u-s-supreme-court (Bloomberg)]
